title: Introduction to Mechatronics

title: Introduction to Mechatronics
text: ELECTRICAL AND ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING Electrical Engineering : Electricity as a power supplier (electric power) for appliances. Also called power electrics. Electronic Engineering : Mainly transmits electric signal and controls some machine by using the electric signal. Also called weak electrics. In mechatronics system, we treat the electric wire that supplies electricity for operations as power electric wire and the wire that transmits signal as weak electric wire.

title: Introduction to Mechatronics
text: COMPUTER Overview of the role of computer • The role of computer is to • translate • the input  electronic signal from the sensors  Keyboard, mouse, distance, temperature… into • the output  electric signal to run the actuators  Display, sound, motor, fan…

title: Introduction to Mechatronics
text: PROGRAM AND MECHATRONICS Most home appliances that use electronic/electrical technology have a built-in computer system called a micro-controller unit (MCU). The MCU is connected to sensors and actuators to form an embedded system that controls operations. A software engineer is mainly in charge of work about embedded system.

text: Sensor Accuracy amount of uncertainty in a measurement with respect to an absolute standard. Effect of errors due to gain and offset parameters.  Offset errors are ◦ given as a unit of measurement such as volts or ohms ◦ independent of the magnitude of the input signal Example: ± 1.0 millivolt (mV)  Gain errors are ◦ do depend on the magnitude of the input signal ◦ are expressed as a percentage of the reading Example: ± 0.1%.

title: Basic knowledge About Sensors (2)
text: Sensor Precision Describes the Reproducibility of the measurement. For example, measure a steady state signal many times.  the values are close together then it has a high degree of precision or repeatability. ◦ The values do not have to be the true values just grouped together. ◦ Take the average of the measurements and the difference between it and the true value is accuracy.

title: Basic knowledge About Sensors (2)
text: Sensor Resolution Can be expressed in 2 ways 1. the ratio between the maximum signal measured to the smallest part that can be resolved - usually with an analog-to-digital (A/D) converter. 2. the degree to which a change can be theoretically detected, usually expressed as a number of bits. In order to determine the resolution of a system in terms of voltage, 1. Assume a system capable of making measurements across a ± 10V range (20V span) using a 16-bits A/D converter. 2. Determine the smallest possible increment we can detect at 16 bits. 2 16 = 65,536, so 20V ÷ 65536 = 305 μ V per A/D count. Therefore, the smallest theoretical change we can detect is 305 μ V.

title: Computer technology required to understand mechatronics
text: FEATURES OF SERIAL COMMUNICATION Features • The sender sends digital information of 0 and 1 one bit at a time in sequence, and then the receiver returns it. • The communication speed of is expressed in bps (Bits Per Second). The speed of 1 bit of data transferred per second is 1 bps. • Important to send at accurate time intervals. • Since the sender side starts sending data without permission, the receiver side needs to accurately identify where the data starts and ends from the received signal. • "synchronization" • By reading the data signal at the timing of the clock signal, the receiving side can acquire data accurately according to the signal of the transmitting side.

title: Computer technology required to understand mechatronics
text: PI IS NOT SO GOOD FOR... • CPU intensive tasks. • I/O intensive apps. title: Computer technology required to understand mechatronics
text: WHAT IS ARDUINO ? • A computer with CPU, RAM, EEPROM, lots of I/O ports. • Programmable via USB. Use the Arduino IDE on a PC. • Programs are stored in EEPROM. EEPROM ( Electrically-Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory)
